- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per subsequent period.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 65–68), model tends to lag; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to forecast for next 3–5 periods.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to counteract downward bias.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price by 1–3% in early 2025 (e.g., 2025-03-17), suggesting persistent lag; apply +1.5% bias to 30d forecast if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67), model may overfit short-term volatility; smooth forecast by reducing volatility amplitude by 10–20%.
